spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation of the Kephalaia Passage

---

**¶2:** Five origins of evil have existed from the beginning in the realm of falsity from evil. The five fundamental forms of evil and falsity poured forth from them. Also, from those five forms of evil were fashioned five kinds of perverted perception. Again, from the five perverted perceptions were fashioned the five genera of evil affections in each infernal state, as to will and as to understanding. And the five infernal states themselves have five ruling evils therein, and five animating falsities, five external forms, five modes of appropriation — in each state, none resembling another.

---

**¶3:** The ruling evil of the state of obscure falsity [GAP-1] which arose from the inmost depths of falsity from evil — this is the one that is the governing principle of all wickedness and all malignity. The beginning of all spiritual assault originated through this ruling evil: all combats, contentions, disputes, perils, devastations, conflicts, and struggles of domination. This is the one who first caused spiritual peril and warfare to arise, with all its infernal states and all its powers. Afterward, it also waged war against divine wisdom. It mounted an assault against the celestial kingdom of divine good.

---

**¶4:** Now, regarding this ruling principle of falsity from evil, there are five qualities upon it. Its governing thought is the lust for dominion from self-love. Its actions and lowest effects are purely demonic evil. Its power is predatory rationality that seizes and devours. Its interior appropriation is the falsification of truth. Its ultimate sensory expression is base corporeal knowing perverted to infernal ends. These five qualities, the marks of its five infernal states, exist upon the ruler of the realms of falsity from evil.

---

**¶5:** Now, there are five further properties in this ruling evil. The first is its utter absence of wisdom. The second is its spiritual putrefaction and corruption. The third is its interior deformity. The fourth is its grievous torment — its own essential life. The fifth is its consuming self-love, which devours like a molten instrument of cruelty, as though poured forth from the fire of the will to dominate.

---

**¶6:** [GAP-2: REVIEW There are] also three further qualities in this ruling evil. The first: that its external form is obstinate and utterly unyielding, even as she has fashioned it — [GAP-3] merciless in its interior will; namely the corporeal mind devoid of spiritual life, which is the thought of spiritual death, [the o]ne who shaped it from the very nature of the realm of falsity from evil. This is the character of the external form of the ruler of obscure falsity. It is more impenetrable than any hardened natural truth, any natural good, any strength of rational argument, or any dense falsity; as there is no principle of discernment at all, nor any instrument of truth, that can [GAP-4] penetrate it and divide it. For the corporeal mind, its fashioner, has formed it [GAP-5] resistant and impenetrable.

---

**¶7:** The second quality: that it wounds and destroys by the utterance of its persuasive falsities. Its doctrinal repetition and its mode of reception, all its irrational teaching, produce enchantment and the binding of minds on its behalf. When it wills, it can pronounce its enchantment upon itself, and by its persuasive falsities conceal itself from its own subordinate evils. Again, when it wills, it can make itself manifest above its powers and appear to them.

---

**¶8:** The third quality: that the ruling principle of the realms of falsity from evil comprehends the thought-forms and modes of communication of its five infernal states. It understands everything it perceives from their expressions, as they communicate with one another, each one in its own mode of thought. [GAP-6: REVIEW Every] design they deliberate against it, every snare they devise among themselves to bring upon it, it knows. It can also understand the covert intentions they signal between one another. Yet its subordinate powers and rulers, who are subject to it, cannot comprehend its own elaborate discourse. While all these things are laid open to it, still, their inmost will is not disclosed to it. It knows not their interior mind nor their thought; it cannot fathom their origin nor their end. Rather, it only knows and apprehends what is immediately present before its sensory awareness.

---

**¶9:** Also, another distinctive quality is found in the ruling principle of the realms of falsity from evil. For when it wills to act, it extends all its influence outward and proceeds. When it reconsiders, it withdraws its influence and contracts it, and is compacted among its subordinate evils; and it falls into the lowest natural plane like a dense cluster and a great mass of impenetrable falsity. It terrifies by its proclamation; it is dreadful. It overwhelms its subordinate powers with its voice — because when it speaks, being like the thunder of persuasive falsity in states of obscurity, it resembles the [GAP-7] shattering of elevated principles [GAP-8]. When it cries out and [GAP-9] and calls [GAP-10] over its powers, they tremble and totter and fall under its domination, even as thoughts of the mind would be [GAP-11] — the thought [GAP-12] — and they fall down to the lowest natural plane. Still, this thing only: it knows not what is remote from its immediate state; it perceives not who is at a distance from it, nor does it apprehend that reality. Rather, whoever is immediately before its presence it perceives, apprehending and knowing it.

---

**¶10:** These signs and these evil qualities are found in the chief of all evils and falsities, the ruler of all the states of self-exaltation in falsity from evil — [GAP-13: the one] to [GAP-14: REVIEW whom] the realm of falsity from evil has given birth, begotten in its cruelty, in its wickedness, and in its wrath [GAP-15].

---

**¶11:** [GAP-16] — surpassing all its fellow ruling evils that exist in all its infernal states.

---

**¶12:** The semblance of celestial good is the external form of the ruler of the realms of falsity from evil. The external form of all the powers belonging to the state of obscure falsity is likewise this semblance of good. And also, the mode by which its works are appropriated is the craving for conjunction of evil with falsity.

---

**¶13:** In contrast, the ruling evil of the states of self-love has the quality of the lust for dominion, the foremost of all evil affections. Perverted natural good is its external form. Again, the external form of all the ruling evils belonging to self-love is perverted natural good. Their mode of appropriation is aversion — the rejection of genuine good that is in every form.

---

**¶14:** Again, the ruling evil of the states of vain reasoning has the quality of predatory intellectual sight. Hardened natural falsity is its external form. Also, the external form of all who belong to vain reasoning is hardened natural falsity. Their mode of appropriation is the cutting, divisive quality of falsity that is in every form.

---

**¶15:** For its part, the ruling evil of the state of perverted truth has the quality of base corporeal knowing. Falsified truth is its external form. All the other ruling evils belonging to perverted truth — falsified truth is their external form. Also, the mode by which their works are appropriated is the deceptive delight of falsified truth, the seductive sweetness that is in every form.

---

**¶16:** Again, [the rul]ing evil of the state of pure falsity is the falsification of all truth. Its [GAP-17: REVIEW external form is the densest, basest falsity] and counterfeit truth. All the other ruling evils [GAP-18: REVIEW who belong to the state of] pure falsity — their external form is dense base falsity and counterfeit truth. And also, the mode by which their works are appropriated is interior torment — the grief of unmixed evil.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Five storehouses have arisen since the beginning in the land of darkness! The five elements poured out of them. Also, from the five elements were fashioned the five trees! Again, from the five trees were fashioned the five genera of creatures in each world, male and female. And the five worlds themselves have five kings therein, and five spirits, five bodies, five tastes; in each world, they not resembling one another!

The King of the world of Smoke [is the one] who came up from the depth of darkness; this is he who is the head of all wickedness, and all malignity. The beginning of the spread of the war occured through him; all the battles, fights, quarrelling, dangers, destructions, fights, wrestling-contests! That is the one who first made arise danger and war, with his worlds and his powers. Afterwards, also, he waged war with the light. He pitched a battle with the exalted kingdom.

Now, regarding the King of Darkness, there are five shapes on him! His head is lion-faced; his hands and feet are demon- and devil-faced; his shoulders are eagle-faced; while his belly is dragon-faced; his tail is fish-faced. These five shapes, the marks of his five worlds, exist on the King of the realms of Darkness!

Now, there are five other properties in him. The first is his darkness. The second is his putridity. The third is his ugliness. The fourth is his bitterness, his own soul. The fifth is his burning, which burns like an iron () as if poured out from fire.

[There are] also three others in him! The first, that his body is hard and very tough, even as she has formed him [fierce and] cruel-hearted; namely Matter, who is the thought of death, [the o]ne who sculpted him from the nature of the land of darkness. This is the manner of the body of the ruler of Smoke. He is harder than every iron, copper and steel and lead; as there is no cleaver at all, nor any iron implement, can [pierce] him and cut him. For Matter, his fashioner, has formed him [to be] strong and hard.

The second, that he wounds and kills by the word of his magic arts. His recitation and hearing, all his foolish instruction, make magic and invocations for him. When it pleases him, he can make an invocation over himself, and by his magic arts be hidden from his companions. Again, when it pleases him, he can be manifested over his powers and appear to them

The third, that the King of the realms of Darkness knows the converse and language of his five worlds. He understands every thing he hears from their mouths, as they address one another; each one of them in his language. [Every] design they will consider against him, every snare they debate with one another to bring upon him, he knows them! He can also understand the gesturing they signal between one another. Yet, his powers and his rulers, who are subject to him, can not understand his wordy converse. While all these things are unveiled to him; still, their heart is not manifested to him. He knows not their mind nor their thought; he can not ponder their beginning and their end. Rather, he only knows and apprehends what is before his eyes.

Also, another different thing is found in the King of the realms of Darkness! For when it pleases him to move, he spreads all his limbs out and walks. When it comes to mind, he with[d]raws his limbs and takes them in, and is rolled (?) to his companions; and he falls to the ground like a grape and a great iron ball! He terrifies by his cry, he is frightful. He frightens his powers with his sound; because when he speaks, being like thunder in the clouds, he resembles the [crashing] of the rocks [in the mountains] When he cries out and [roars] and calls [with his voice] over his powers, they shall tremble and to[tter a]nd fall under foot; even as some birds would be [frightened by] the bird [ ... / ... ] and they fall down to the earth. Still, this thing only: he knows not what is far from him, he sees not who is at a distance, nor does he hear him. Rather, whoever is before his face he sees, hearing him and knowing him.

These signs and these evil marks are found in the chief of the demons and fiends, the King of all the mountains of Darkness [He is the one] to [whom] the land of darkness has given birth, begotten in its cruelty, in its wickedness and its wrath [against the light]
[He has all these] more than all his fellow rulers, who are in all his worlds.
Gold is the body of the King of the realms of Darkness. The body of all the powers who belong to the world of Smoke is gold. And also, the taste of its fruits is salty.

In contrast, the King of the worlds of Fire is lion-faced, the foremost of all the beasts. Copper is his body. Again, the body of all the rulers who belong to Fire is copper. Their taste is the sour taste that is in every form.
Again, the King of the worlds of Wind is eagle-face. His body is iron. Also, the body of all they who belong to the Wind is iron. Their taste is the sharp taste that is in every form.

For his part, the King of the world of Water is fish-face. His body is silver. All the other rulers who belong to Water, silver is their body. Also, the taste of their fruit is the sweetness of water, the sweet taste that is in every (form).

Again, [the Kin]g of the world of Darkness is a dragon. His [body is lead] and tin. All the other rulers [who belong to the world of] Darkness, their body is lead and tin. And also, the taste of their fruits is bitterness.

fills.explanation: The passage identifies the King of Smoke as the chief adversary, and "is the one who came up from the depth" parallels the next clause "this is he who is the head of all wickedness," establishing the formulaic identification pattern used throughout the Kephalaia.
The editor's choice "There are" matches the standard Kephalaia formulaic opener for introducing new enumerated properties, consistent with the pattern in ¶5 and throughout the chapter.

The spiritual reading indicates the gap describes a quality paired with "cruel-hearted" (merciless in interior will); "fierce and cruel-hearted" creates the natural pair of outward ferocity and inward mercilessness that characterizes the ruler's unyielding external form as fashioned by Matter.

The spiritual reading says "penetrate it and divide it"; in the natural-plane vocabulary of iron implements, "pierce" pairs naturally with "cut" as two complementary modes of attack with weapons, and corresponds to the spiritual reality of no truth being able to penetrate this evil.

The construction "has formed him to be strong and hard" is the natural infinitive complement in the Kephalaia's expository register, indicating the purposive result of Matter's fashioning, corresponding to the spiritual reality of being made resistant and impenetrable.

The editor's "Every" is confirmed; it fits the universal quantifier pattern used throughout this paragraph to describe the King's comprehensive knowledge of his subordinates' schemes ("every design... every snare").

The spiritual reading indicates "shattering of elevated principles"; in the natural-plane vocabulary of the rock simile following the thunder comparison, "crashing" captures both the violent sound and the destructive force of rocks — the natural-plane equivalent of shattering.

The rock simile naturally completes with a location; "in the mountains" fits both the Kephalaia's recurring image of the "mountains of Darkness" (¶10) and the natural imagery of rocks crashing in mountains, paralleling the thunder-in-clouds comparison.

The triadic vocalization pattern "cries out and [X] and calls" requires a parallel verb of terrifying utterance; "roars" fits the lion-headed King perfectly and corresponds to the spiritual reality of the ruling evil's overwhelming proclamation.

The passage emphasizes the King's terrifying sound ("his cry," "his sound," "thunder"); "calls with his voice over his powers" completes the vocalization triad by specifying the instrument of his command, consistent with the preceding and following references to his voice and cry.

The simile compares the powers trembling and falling to small birds reacting to a predatory bird; "frightened by" supplies the passive verb of terror that connects the small birds to the predatory bird, matching the theme of the King terrifying his subordinates.

The passage transitions from summarizing the King's evil marks to identifying him as the one born from darkness; "He is the one to whom the land of darkness has given birth" provides the natural demonstrative identification consistent with the Kephalaia's formulaic style.
The editor's "whom" is grammatically required as the relative pronoun governed by the verb "has given birth to," forming "the one to whom the land of darkness has given birth."

The concluding phrase specifies the direction of the land of darkness's wrath, tying back to ¶3's central theme that the King "waged war with the light" and "pitched a battle with the exalted kingdom"; the wrath of darkness is fundamentally oriented against the light.

Paragraph 11 summarizes the King's superiority; "He has all these more than all his fellow rulers" echoes ¶10's summary of "these signs and these evil marks" and states his preeminence, matching the spiritual reading's "surpassing all its fellow ruling evils."

The editor's "body is lead" follows the exact pattern of ¶12–15 where each king's body corresponds to a metal (gold, copper, iron, silver); lead corresponds to the world of Darkness as the densest, basest metal, matching Swedenborg's correspondence of lead with dense falsity.
